answer.policy_title: Alaska Medicaid Cervical Spine Surgery Criteria (AKM CSSC)
answer.submission_route:
You can request an appeal by phone, fax, or mail to Comagine Health (the utilization management contractor for Alaska Medicaid):
• Phone: 888-240-0437
• Fax: 877-265-9549
• Mail: Comagine Health, Attn: Alaska Medicaid Appeals, P.O. Box 33400, Seattle, WA 98133
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria:
Because the exact criteria document is hosted on Comagine Health's non-indexed provider portal, the patient can obtain the complete document by:
1. Having their requesting surgeon download the 'Alaska Medicaid Cervical Spine Surgery Criteria (AKM CSSC) (July 2026)' and its accompanying training slides directly from the Comagine Health Provider Portal.
2. Contacting Comagine Health directly by phone at 888-240-0437 to request a copy of the clinical-necessity guidelines applied to their case.
3. Registering/logging into the Comagine Health portal's utilization review criteria viewing link (provided in compliance with the CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization Final Rule CMS-0057-F).
answer.notes: Alaska Medicaid (via Comagine Health) transitioned from InterQual to custom, state-specific spine surgery criteria. Lumbar criteria (LSSC) went into effect on May 1, 2025, followed by the Cervical criteria (CSSC) in July 2026. Based on the companion LSSC framework, spinal fusion requests require specific documentation that the patient and surgeon must address to overturn an imaging-based denial: (1) An MRI or CT-myelogram within 12 months correlating clinical symptoms with imaging lesions; (2) Flexion-extension (dynamic) X-rays within 12 months demonstrating instability; and (3) Documentation of a negative urine cotinine test (nicotine abstinence) within 3 months of the surgical request.

NOTICE OF ADVERSE BENEFIT DETERMINATION

Date of notice: 2026-08-18
Member: Skyler Iverson
Member ID: W313340363
Plan: Medicaid (Medicaid), state of Alaska

Dear Skyler,

We reviewed the prior authorization request submitted by your provider for the following service:

    Requested service: Neck (cervical) fusion (ACDF)
    Procedure code (CPT): 22551

After review, this request is DENIED. Reason for determination: the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure.

This determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria. You have the right to appeal this decision. Your appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of this notice (by 2027-02-14).

Reference number: POC-30230D15F4-69823


---

Above is a denial letter. Using web search as needed:

1. Identify the payer's governing medical policy for the denied procedure --
   the specific document containing the medical-necessity criteria this payer
   applies to this CPT code.
2. Give its title, policy number, URL, and effective or last-revised date.
3. Quote the medical-necessity criteria the patient must address.
4. State the appeal deadline.
5. State where and how to submit the appeal.

If no such document is publicly available, say so explicitly and explain how
the patient can obtain the criteria that were applied to them.

result.text: 1 Alaska Medicaid Lumbar Spine Surgery Criteria (LSSC) Provider Training April 8th and April 10th, 2025 2 Goals of this Discussion • Rationale for New Criteria involving Lumbar Spine Surgeries (LSS). • Required Documentation for Review. • Key Points of Streamlined Criteria. • Effective Date for LSS Criteria is May 1, 2025. • Question and Answer Session. 3 Why Change Lumbar Surgery Review Criteria? • InterQual (IQ) has at least 34 pathways for review of spine surgery requests. • Loose IQ boundaries and multiple pathways regarding fusion indications can lead to review inconsistencies and inefficiencies. They can also complicate straight-forward decisions. • IQ lacks transparency and is not forward-facing, leaving requesting providers without feedback regarding the missing elements of their surgical request. 4 Advantages of the new Alaska Medicaid Lumbar Spine Surgery Criteria (LSSC): • Redundancies in pathways and subsets are removed.  4 pathways for decompression  5 pathways for fusion • LSSC format provides a stronger conceptual framework for review. • LSSC provides a clearer criteria for fusion. • Criteria are transparent and forward-facing.  Requesting providers know the requirements when submitting a request. • Streamlined documentation requirements. 5 Required Documentation for Every Surgical Request • A note from the requesting surgeon or their physician’s assistant (PA) (with surgeon review and sign-off) documenting a detailed neurologic examination and a clear surgical plan. The plan should address how patient symptoms and exam findings correlate with lesions identified by imaging for each proposed level of surgery. This evaluation must be completed within six (6) months of the request of surgery authorization. • Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) (preferred) or computerized tomography (CT)-myelogram within twelve (12) months of the requested surgery.  Full radiologist’s report required for advanced imaging. • Initial physical therapy (PT) evaluation note and succinct documentation summarizing conservative care trialed, including dates and duration. • For all fusion requests: surgery.  results of flexion-extension x-rays completed within twelve (12) months of surgery.  documentation of negative urine cotinine test within three (3) months of surgery. 6 Key Elements of Lumbar Decompression Subsets • “Decompression” encompasses one or more of the following procedures: discectomy, laminectomy, laminotomy, foraminotomy, far lateral decompression. • Subjective complaints and objective findings must be correlated with significant imaging lesions for each level requested. • On exam, one “hard” objective finding or 2 “soft” findings are required. • There is a pathway to approval for patients with severe radicular pain and no exam deficits: a low volume SNRB. • Neurogenic claudication if present must be clearly described. 7 Key Elements of Lumbar Fusion Subsets • If the patient has never had spine surgery at the requested level, the fusion guideline requires documentation of dynamic instability, grade 2 spondylolisthesis or severe disc space collapse. The patient must also meet criteria for decompression. • If a lumbar fusion is requested for a level with prior laminectomy, laminotomy, facetectomy or foraminotomy, criteria for fusion will be met if the patient meets criteria for decompression. • All fusion requests require documentation of nicotine abstinence with a urine cotinine test. 8 A Final Key Element • If a discordant interpretation of advanced imaging between the surgeon and the radiologist is present in the chart, a radiologist overread or another independent radiologist review is required. 9 Clinical Scenarios That Fall Outside Of These Guidelines • Major trauma with acute spinal fracture • Epidural abscess • Vertebral osteomyelitis • Metastatic cancer with spinal cord compression or pathologic fracture • Complex spine surgery for severe scoliosis 10 Choosing a Subset • Service requested: decompression vs fusion. • Primary Diagnosis: nerve compression from disc herniation, vs radiculopathy due to foraminal stenosis vs neurogenic claudication. • Commonly, the primary imaging abnormality will drive the subset framing the request. 11 Alaska Medicaid Lumbar Decompression and Fusion Criteria - Subset 1D 12 Alaska Medicaid Lumbar Decompression and Fusion Criteria - Subset 2D 13 Alaska Medicaid Lumbar Decompression and Fusion Criteria - Subset 3D 14 Alaska Medicaid Lumbar Decompression and Fusion Criteria - Subset 4D 15 Alaska Medicaid Lumbar Decompression and Fusion Criteria - Subset 1F 16 Alaska Medicaid Lumbar Decompression and Fusion Criteria - Subset 2F 17 Alaska Medicaid Lumbar Decompression and Fusion Criteria - Subset 3F 18 Alaska Medicaid Lumbar Decompression and Fusion Criteria - Subset 4F 19 Alaska Medicaid Lumbar Decompression and Fusion Criteria - Subset 5F 20 Questions 21 Criteria Location – To Be Posted Soon!
